accepted_contract: Real acknowledgements reread and lock the same persisted order as stream/recovery, reject changed broker identity, validate the original client/symbol/side/quantity and apply the shared atomic fill transaction.

First real nested filled acknowledgement creates Execution/lot/audit effects once; late/stale snapshots cannot erase established fills or reopen terminal/partial summaries. Equal-quantity cash correction remains explicit.
Synthetic mode metadata cannot relabel a persisted real broker identity. Existing first synthetic acknowledgement compatibility remains.

Known real broker success followed by local accounting or delivery-status persistence failure latches original-client lookup-only state before the next persistence await. A restarted worker uses GET only; exhaustion broadcasts reconciliation-required rather than falsely rejected.
No submission/cancellation/retry-policy change; only three authorized worker method ASTs differ. Shared validator was previously independently reviewed by the accounting owner.
findings_closed: Partial-fill status could be demoted by a no-new-fill generic acknowledgement; final guard and regression preserve it.
Mode flip to synthetic acknowledgement could relabel a real order; final identity/mode guard and four regressions reject it.
Post-success persistence failures formerly lost known acknowledgement classification and could falsely broadcast rejection; final wrapper and sent-commit latches retain the durable existing protocol.
limitations: Overlapping suites are not additive unique platform coverage.
Actual PostgreSQL lock wait and cumulative fill cases are bounded concurrency evidence, not a stress or distributed exactly-once certification.
A crash/cancellation or total durable-write failure before the lookup-only marker commits remains a broker/local persistence window; no atomic broker/database guarantee.
No runtime, real broker, production database, credentials, models or active freeze state were accessed or changed by this review.
